requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: Changes how TypeCollector handles bad keys. After reporting a mixed int/string key diagnostic, it now skips that member with `continue` (lines 1008, 1148). It also stops adding a second member with an already-used int or string key, using a ContainsKey guard (lines 1023-1026, 1039-1042, 1163-1166). Previously these paths could throw: `intKey!.Value` was read with a null key, and Dictionary.Add threw on a duplicate key. The change adds analyzer tests for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types, a runtime round-trip execution test, and a README section describing which diagnostics apply to suppressed types.
story.why: Issue #2234: since 3.1.1 the analyzer stops reporting diagnostics on `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types. The diff's implied root cause is that the analyzer threw while collecting members with bad keys.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new user-facing 'Opting out of source generation' section. It promises which rules do and do not fire for suppressed types.
A new execution test checks runtime serialization of a suppressed type through the dynamic resolver. This is not analyzer behavior.
The crash fixes also change behavior for ordinary, non-suppressed [MessagePackObject] types (see DuplicateKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailureForGeneratedTypes).
story.confidence_overview: High that the edited lines remove specific throw paths: a null `intKey!.Value` and a duplicate-key Dictionary.Add. Medium-to-low that this is the actual cause of #2234. No line in the diff mentions SuppressSourceGeneration, and the visible lines do not show why suppressed types were affected and generated types were not. The unchanged code that decides whether suppressed types are analyzed at all is not visible.

findings.description: No changed line refers to SuppressSourceGeneration. The fix is a generic crash guard that also applies to generated types. The diff does not explain why 3.1.0 worked and 3.1.1 broke only for suppressed types. If the regression is an early return or skip for suppressed types elsewhere, that code is untouched. MemberWithoutKeyIsReported and the similar tests would then still fail, or they already passed and do not test the regression.

`continue` after the mixed-key diagnostic skips the rest of the per-member processing for that member. That includes the formatter-attribute lookup and, possibly, member-type checks such as MsgPack003. Some other diagnostics on that member may no longer be reported.

Duplicate int keys are now dropped silently at the point of insertion. This is safe only if a MsgPack005 diagnostic is reported for the duplicate elsewhere; that check is outside the visible hunk (lines 1012-1018). If it is not reported, the generator could emit a formatter missing a member without any error. The tests expect MsgPack005, which suggests it is reported.
The README promises that MsgPack012 is reported for suppressed types, but no test in the diff covers MsgPack012 on a suppressed type.
